bands.d: You are ahead of most teams we see. Keep the data map current as you add features and vendors, and re-run this whenever a new integration starts touching personal data.
The foundations are there. Close the remaining controls in order — data map first, then consent capture, then withdrawal and deletion — and you will be in good shape well before enforcement.

You have started, but the unchecked items include things that take engineering time rather than paperwork. Sequence them: map your data, fix consent capture so the problem stops growing, then build withdrawal and deletion.

A low score here is common and fixable, but not on a short timeline. Begin by documenting every field you collect and where it flows — every other control depends on that being right, and it is usually faster than teams expect.

items.t: We can list every personal data field we collect, and why
items.s: A current data map covering the app, backend, analytics and third-party tools

items.t: Consent is unbundled — separate opt-in per purpose
items.s: Analytics, marketing, location and sharing each asked for separately, defaulted off

items.t: Our consent notice is in plain language
items.s: Readable by a normal user, not only by a lawyer

items.t: Users can withdraw consent as easily as they gave it
items.s: A settings screen with per-purpose toggles, not an email to support
The signal propagates to analytics, CRM and any third parties

items.t: We can fully delete a user on request
items.s: Including analytics, backups, logs and SaaS tools — not a soft-delete flag

items.t: We have defined retention periods and enforce them
items.s: Automated deletion jobs rather than keeping everything indefinitely

items.t: We have a path for children's data
items.s: Age assurance and verifiable parental consent if under-18s may use the app

items.t: We would detect a breach and know who was affected
items.s: Logging and alerting good enough to notify the Board and users in time

items.t: Our vendor contracts cover data processing
items.s: Written terms with every processor that touches personal data

footnote: Nothing you tick is sent anywhere — this runs entirely in your browser.
